correctness.rationale: Root-order-ideal decomposition gives exact Fourier product recursion. Parity proves odd-height nonvanishing; product-zero/unit counting proves the even-height null fraction recursion. The d<=6 global inequality is established by all-positive exact rational Bernstein coefficients (degree at most 35; standalone code), and d>=7 by an exact Bernoulli witness plus the monotone one-turning-point ratio. Independent exact Walsh-transform enumeration verifies all frequency coefficients for (d,h)=(2,0..3),(3,0..2). No finite experiment is used to infer an infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison with the primary tree hard-core mixing paper, general Boolean Fourier convolution text, related published tree-colouring Fourier conditioning, ideal-lattice counting and graph-exclusion interpolation yielded no equivalent or stronger implication. The derived polynomial map and its exact seven-branch threshold are not among the checked results; unindexed signed tree-poset generating functions remain a specific residual priority risk. The accessible product-of-two-chains ideal theorem is compared directly: its modulo-four law and vanishing zero density cannot imply a positive limit for complete d-ary rooted trees.
residual_risks: No exhaustive search of historic signed order-ideal multivariate enumerators or unpublished dissertations; an unindexed equivalent fixed-point recurrence may exist.
